• 60s: The Kinks. "But wait," you say. "everyone knows the Kinks." Well, everyone knows Lola and You Really Got Me... but during the British Invasion, the Kinks were up there with the Beatles and Stones. Most of that material never sold well or got airplay outside of Britain.

  • 70s: The Jam were another great band that was big in Britain but never really crossed over. They rode the early punk wave, but like their peers The Clash, were smarter and better musicians than a lot of the punk genre, but I've rarely met anyone outside of the UK who knows who The Jam or Paul Weller are.

  • 80s: Spacemen 3 was the group Jason Spaceman was in before Spiritualized, and they were damn good. Similar themes of drugs, drone, gospel, and pre-punk. edit: Good starters: Playing with Fire, The Perfect Prescription. Their first album, Sound of Confusion, is also good but very garage, so maybe not the best starter if you didn't like Nuggets.

  • 90s: Concrete Blonde was a California rock band that had a couple of hit singles (e.g., Bloodletting) but never really broke into the big time. Most of their stuff is worth a listen, especially the first 3-4 albums.

  • 00s: James McMurtry is kind of like if Leonard Cohen was a Texas cowboy and played electric guitar.

  • 10s: Hm, this is kind of tough. Maybe Ty Segall; I wouldn't say he's underrated per se but he deserves a lot more fame than he's got.
